# UX & Accessibility Checklist: Dark Mode Toggle

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the UX and accessibility requirements for the dark mode toggle (clarity, completeness, consistency, measurability) before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Toggle Control Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Is the toggle's placement specified as a requirement, not only as an assumption ("page header")? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK002 Is "visible toggle" defined with measurable properties (minimum size, label or icon, position relative to other header content)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the visual states of the toggle itself (light-active, dark-active) specified, including how each state is distinguished without relying on color alone? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the toggle's visible label or icon content defined, including whether it shows the current state or the state it will switch to? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK005 Are interaction state requirements (hover, focus, active, disabled) defined for the toggle in both appearances? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the minimum size of the toggle's interactive target specified for touch use? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK007 Are narrow-viewport / mobile layout requirements for the header toggle defined? [Gap]

## Appearance & Visual Requirements

- [ ] CHK008 Are the "dark appearance" colors defined or constrained (palette, background/surface/text roles), or is that explicitly deferred to planning? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the list of elements covered by "entire app" enumerated, including any elements not named (empty state, buttons, inputs, placeholders, borders, scrollbars)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the "all states of a todo" listed (active, completed, hover, focus, editing, deleting)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "clearly distinguishable" for active vs completed todos quantified or tied to a measurable criterion? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the requirement that light "stays unchanged" measurable, such as a reference for what counts as unchanged? [Measurability, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for native browser UI that follows the appearance (form controls, scrollbars, text selection color)? [Gap]

## Transition & Timing Requirements

- [ ] CHK014 Is "immediately" defined consistently between the acceptance scenarios and the 100 ms success criterion? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK015 Is it specified whether the change animates or switches instantly, including behavior for users who prefer reduced motion? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the 100 ms threshold in SC-002 defined with a measurement point (input event to first painted frame) and a reference environment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Is "no flash of the wrong appearance" defined in measurable terms, since SC-003 states "zero visible flashes" without a detection method? [Measurability, Spec §FR-004, SC-003]

## Accessibility Requirements

- [ ] CHK018 Is the toggle's accessible name specified, and does it stay stable as the state changes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Is "current state to assistive technology" specified precisely (for example, state exposed as pressed/checked rather than a changing label)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for announcing the appearance change to screen reader users after activation? [Gap, Spec §US3 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK021 Is "standard activation key" enumerated (Enter, Space) for the toggle's control type? [Ambiguity, Spec §US3 Scenario 2]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the toggle's position in the tab order defined relative to the other header and form controls? [Clarity, Spec §US3 Scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK023 Are focus indicator requirements measurable (minimum contrast against adjacent colors, minimum thickness) in both appearances? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the 4.5:1 contrast requirement extended to non-text UI (toggle boundary, focus ring, completed-todo styling), or is the scope limited to text? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK025 Is a contrast threshold specified for large text and for non-text components, since the spec only states 4.5:1 for text? [Gap, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK026 Is it specified whether completed-todo text (typically dimmed) must also meet 4.5:1 in both appearances? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, US1 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the "every piece of text and every control" scope in SC-004 consistent with the narrower wording in FR-007? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements stated for forced-colors / high-contrast operating system modes? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the WCAG version and level (2.x AA from the constitution) referenced in the spec so the accessibility criteria are traceable? [Traceability, Spec §FR-007]

## Default & Preference Behavior

- [ ] CHK030 Are requirements defined for the system setting changing while the app is open and no explicit choice has been saved? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK031 Is it clear what the toggle shows on first visit (the system-derived appearance) and that its state matches what is displayed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, FR-006]
- [ ] CHK032 Is there a requirement for how a user returns to "follow the system" after choosing explicitly, or is its absence an intentional exclusion? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK033 Is behavior defined when the system setting is unavailable or reports no preference? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements consistent between "falls back to the first-visit default" for corrupted preferences and the "no saved choice" rule? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-005]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the user-facing behavior defined when the preference cannot be saved (no indication vs a notice)? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK036 Are multi-tab requirements defined (a change in one open tab while another is open)? [Gap, Coverage]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK037 Are requirements defined for content added while in dark mode (a new todo, an error or empty state) so it uses the active appearance from the first moment? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the rapid-toggle requirement ("no intermediate state sticks") defined in terms observable by the user and the saved preference? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK039 Is "without visible delay" for very large lists consistent with the 500-todo bound in SC-002? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK040 Are print and non-screen exclusions stated consistently, including whether a printed page follows the chosen appearance? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Success Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK041 Can SC-001 ("under 5 seconds on first try, no instructions") be objectively verified, with the participant group and success definition stated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK042 Does every UX-relevant functional requirement trace to at least one success criterion or acceptance scenario? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK043 Are the requirements for FR-009 (no change to todo data) and the "all states of a todo" scope in FR-002 free of conflict about what may change visually? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, FR-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
